raw_response:
I'll think through this like the farmer I am.

---

OK, 50 mu is a lot of cabbage. I've been doing three rounds of cabbage every year for 5 years now — spring, summer, autumn. In Quzhou a lot of us grow cabbage for the Beijing and Shijiazhuang markets, so this is what I know.

Last year my spring crop did OK, maybe 5000 kg per mu. Summer cabbage is always hardest — heat, worms, bolting — I only got about 4000 kg. Autumn is my best season, usually 6000 kg if the weather holds. I'll plan based on that.

**Seeds:** I use hybrid seed, always. The neighbors who stick with old varieties get smaller heads and more disease. I buy from the dealer in town — "中甘" type for spring and autumn, heat-tolerant "夏宝" kind for summer. Costs more but the heads are uniform and traders pay better.

**Fertilizer:** Cabbage eats a lot, especially nitrogen and potassium. I base fertilizer off what I did last year. For each cabbage crop I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, about 50 kg per mu, then top-dress with urea twice during heading. That gives me roughly 25 kg N, 8 kg P, 15 kg K per mu for spring and autumn. Summer crop I push a little less N because too much leaves invite worms and soft rot — maybe 22 kg. Potassium I try to keep up because it helps the heads firm up and store better.

I know some say you can cut nitrogen, but I'd rather spend the extra 30-40 yuan per mu than have loose heads that don't sell. A bad harvest on 50 mu is a disaster.

**Water:** Well irrigation, so I control it myself. Spring I water maybe 5 times. Summer is rainy sometimes so 4 times usually enough, but if July is dry I go 6. Autumn 6 times — the heading stage needs steady moisture.

**Pesticide:** Cabbage has so many pests here — diamondback moth, cabbage worm, aphids. Summer is the worst. I spray about 5 times in spring, 7-8 in summer, 5 in autumn. I rotate products so the worms don't get used to one kind. Input dealer tells me which new ones to try.

**Tillage:** I plough deep before spring planting to break up the soil and bury residue, then rotary between crops. Don't have time for no-till with three crops a year.

50 mu means I hire help for transplanting and harvest — can't do it with just my family of 4. That's a big cost, so I need yields to hold up.
